captions.detailed: A 3D-printable multi-part bicycle light mount consisting of two main clamp assemblies. On one side, there are two identical pairs of handlebar clamps featuring extended drops with integrated pivot bolt holes for connecting to the light bracket. On the other side is a larger, taller cylindrical flashlight clamp split down the middle, complete with side mounting flanges, structural triangular ribs, and a perpendicular bottom pivot barrel for adjustable angle mounting.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric bicycle light mount in OpenSCAD that clamps onto a handlebar and holds a flashlight. The design should feature a two-part handlebar clamp with an adjustable drop length and bolt holes, and a separate, larger cylindrical flashlight clamp with reinforced support flanges and an integrated pivot bracket to allow angle adjustment.
captions.factory: The code defines several modules to build the mount parts. 'HandlebarClamp' uses a difference of a union (cylinder and cube) with a central handlebar cylinder cut, bolt shaft/cap cuts, and a split-half cube. 'HandlebarClampDrop' extends this clamp by using a 'hull' of a circle and square, extruded via 'linear_extrude' to form the drop arm, complete with a pivot bolt hole. 'LightClampWithSupport' and 'LightClampWithBoltMount' construct the flashlight holder using nested cylinders, cubes, linear-extruded helper triangles, and horizontal bolt-hole cylinders. The final layout translates and mirrors these components to output printable halves of each clamp.
